title: Oven BBQ Back Ribs with Buttered Corn
subtitle: pork back ribs slow-baked in foil until tender, then glazed with homemade barbecue sauce, with buttery corn on the cob
imageAlt: A rack of glossy barbecue pork ribs cut into pieces beside buttered corn on the cob on a white plate with a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: The ribs bake low and slow for 2½ hours wrapped in foil, then get glazed in a hot oven. Mostly hands-off.
Peel the thin membrane off the bone side: lift a corner with a butter knife and pull it off with a paper towel.

steps.title: Rub
steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C (300°F). Peel the membrane off the ribs. Mix the 2 tbsp brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt and pepper and rub it all over.

steps.title: Bake low
steps.text: Wrap each rack tightly in foil, meat side up, and bake on a rimmed baking sheet 2½ hours, until the meat is tender and pulling back from the bones (well past 71°C / 160°F).

steps.title: BBQ sauce
steps.text: Near the end, simmer the ketchup, ¼ cup brown sugar, vinegar, Worcestershire and garlic powder in a small pot 5 minutes, until slightly thick.

steps.title: Glaze
steps.text: Turn the oven up to 230°C (450°F). Open the foil, pour off the juices, brush the ribs generously with sauce and bake uncovered 10–12 minutes, until sticky and caramelised at the edges.

steps.title: Corn
steps.text: While the ribs glaze, boil the corn in a large pot 5–6 minutes. Drain and roll in the butter and salt.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Rest the ribs 5 minutes, cut between the bones and serve with the corn and the rest of the sauce.

fixIt.fix: They need more time, not more heat: wrap them again and bake 20–30 minutes more.
Brush it on only for the last 10–12 minutes; the sugar scorches if it goes on early.
That's a good problem. Cut with a sharp knife, bone side up.

saleTip: Back ribs are often $8.80/kg at No Frills, cheaper in summer barbecue sales; they freeze well wrapped tight.
swap: Side ribs: meatier and cheaper; bake 3 hours wrapped.
leftovers: Cut into single bones; reheat covered with a spoon of sauce.
doneness: Pork to at least 71°C (160°F) (Health Canada, pork); ribs are baked on to about 90°C (195°F) so they're tender.
source: Based on tested oven-baked back rib methods (Canadian Living, America's Test Kitchen): dry-rubbed ribs wrapped in foil at 150°C for about 2½ hours, then sauced and glazed uncovered in a hot oven.
prepAhead: Rub the ribs the night before and keep them wrapped in the fridge.
Bake the ribs in foil a day ahead and chill; glaze at 230°C (450°F) for 15 minutes, until 74°C (165°F).
reheat: Covered with a spoon of sauce at 180°C (350°F) for 15–20 minutes, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Rubbed ribs with the barbecue sauce; no corn.

addSteps.title: Coleslaw
addSteps.text: Stir the mayonnaise, vinegar, sugar and a pinch of salt together and toss with the coleslaw mix. Chill until serving.

plating: Ribs stacked on a board, cut side up.
Extra sauce in a small dish and plenty of napkins.

why.0-0: Low heat in foil melts the connective tissue so the meat goes tender without drying out.
why.1-1: Sugar in the sauce caramelises in the hot oven into that sticky glaze.
why.1-2: Vinegar cuts the richness and balances the sweet sauce.

funFact: Back ribs, also called baby back ribs, come from where the rib meets the spine, under the loin; 'baby' just means they're shorter than spare ribs.

keeps.note: freeze the ribs with a little sauce
